name: ls
purpose: List files and folders present in the current directory.
explanation: Displays the files and folders in your current location only; it does not automatically look inside subfolders. If a folder is empty, ls prints nothing (blank).

parameters.description: Long/detailed listing showing permissions (e.g. -rw-r--r--), owner, size, and date.
Shows all files, including hidden files starting with a dot (e.g. .git).
Combines -l and -a for a detailed listing including hidden files.

whenToUse: To inspect what files or directories exist in your current folder or check file permissions.
commonMistakes: Thinking ls failed when it prints nothing in an empty directory.
Forgetting -a when looking for hidden folders like .git.
